Mask small partial correlations to zero

Source: R/edge_probs.R
mask_pcor.Rd

Posterior mean partial correlations of each group, with the edges that select_edges() does not select set to zero: by default the magnitude rule \(P(|\rho_{ij}| > c)\) with Bayesian FDR control. Use it to report or draw each group's network.

Usage

mask_pcor(
  fit,
  c = NULL,
  rule = "magnitude",
  alpha = 0.05,
  decision = NULL,
  level = 0.5,
  groups = NULL,
  chain = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list.

c

Threshold on the partial-correlation scale (one value, or one per group), for rule = "magnitude".

rule, alpha, decision, level

Passed to select_edges(). Any rule of select_edges() can be used, e.g. "structural" (G-Wishart, SSVS) or "shrinkage" (mGHS).

groups

Groups to mask (default all).

chain

NULL (default) pools chains.

Value

An array [p, p, K] of masked posterior mean partial correlations (unit diagonal), with attributes c (per group), rule and n_selected.

Details

Not for differential analysis. Comparing masked networks turns "selected in one group, not in the other" into a difference, even when the two partial correlations are almost equal (one just above \(c\), one just below). Call differences with select_diff_edges() on the unmasked posterior, with \(c\) from calibrate_c().

See also

select_edges(), select_diff_edges()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 80, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                     burnin = 100, nsave = 100, save_draws = FALSE)
m <- mask_pcor(fit, c = 0.1)
round(m[, , 1], 2)
#>       [,1] [,2]  [,3] [,4] [,5]  [,6]
#> [1,]  1.00    0 -0.33    0 0.00  0.00
#> [2,]  0.00    1  0.00    0 0.00  0.00
#> [3,] -0.33    0  1.00    0 0.00 -0.38
#> [4,]  0.00    0  0.00    1 0.00  0.00
#> [5,]  0.00    0  0.00    0 1.00  0.39
#> [6,]  0.00    0 -0.38    0 0.39  1.00
